justification: Frontend-only: draw the lot boundary on the brief's aerial. Fetches the WGS84 GeoJSON lot polygon from the existing /api/property/profile route (the same source PropertyProfile and the granny-flat tool use) and passes it to the existing AerialTile lotPolygon prop. No new component, no new data source, no new conversion.

pre_impl.existing_data: AerialTile already accepts a lotPolygon prop and draws the outline; /api/property/profile already returns lat, lng and a WGS84 lotPolygon (Web Mercator rings converted server-side). PropertyProfile already consumes exactly this. The brief was passing only lat/lng.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The aerial showed the area but not the actual block outline; the data and the rendering capability already existed and just needed wiring, not new code.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new component, API, or conversion. Adds a lotPolygon state, a useEffect that fetches /api/property/profile for the resolved address and stores data.lotPolygon, and passes it to AerialTile. handleReset clears it.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The fetch is wrapped: a non-ok response or a thrown error leaves lotPolygon null, so AerialTile falls back to its centered-aerial (no overlay) exactly as before.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Frontend only (TypeScript/React). lotPolygon is typed {type:'Polygon';coordinates:number[][][]}|null; the effect guards on address and state and cancels on unmount; AerialTile already types the prop.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: the aerial was just a centered photo. After: the actual lot boundary is outlined on it; if the polygon can't be fetched, it gracefully shows the photo without the outline.

functions.name: IntelligenceBriefInner
functions.input: renders the Intelligence Brief page; now also resolves the lot polygon for the aerial overlay
functions.output: the brief UI including an aerial with the lot boundary drawn when the polygon is available
functions.if_none: if the lot polygon fetch fails or returns nothing, lotPolygon stays null and the aerial renders without an overlay

values: N/A - no regulatory values. The lot polygon is geometry from the existing property API; nothing is hardcoded.
queries: N/A for new queries - reuses the existing /api/property/profile route; no new database or API endpoint is added.

break_it.scenario: The property profile fetch fails or returns no lotPolygon
break_it.what_happens: a naive overlay could crash the map or render an empty shape
break_it.repro: the fetch is wrapped in catch and the success path only sets state when d.lotPolygon is present; otherwise lotPolygon stays null
break_it.how: AerialTile renders the centered aerial without an overlay when lotPolygon is null, exactly as before

break_it.scenario: The user resets and runs a new brief for a different address
break_it.what_happens: a stale lot boundary from the previous address could draw over the new aerial
break_it.repro: handleReset calls setLotPolygon(null); the effect re-fetches for the new resolved address
break_it.how: the polygon is cleared on reset and the effect, keyed on the address, fetches the new one

break_it.scenario: The effect fires repeatedly or after unmount during streaming
break_it.what_happens: a late response could set state on an unmounted component or thrash
break_it.repro: the effect uses a cancelled flag and only runs in streaming/complete with an address
break_it.how: the cleanup sets cancelled = true so a late response is ignored, and the deps key it to the address and state

post_merge.manual_verify: On the brief, confirm the aerial now shows the lot outline (teal) over the property; for an address whose polygon can't be fetched, the aerial still renders without the outline.
